messages.subject: Re: Species metadata tag not found
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
please don't use spaces in the tag group names. While digiKam allows it, camtrapR has problems with it. This is because the tag group name ("Common name" in your case) is used as a column name, and R normally does not like spaces in column names. Therefore, to be on the safe side, camtrapR expects no spaces in the metadataSpeciesTag.
I'll add a proper warning for that.
It is also mentioned in vignette 2. The good news is that you can rename the tag group in digiKam and batch-update the metadata of all images. See vignette 2, under "What if non-hierarchical metadata tags were assigned to images already?", points 4 and 5.
Cheers,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: recordTable on subset of directories
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
currently that is not implemented, sorry. recordTable searches all subdirectories of inDir. I also never considered such an extreme case, and I am astonished the function ran for days (would have thought hours at most).
Just to be sure I understand you correctly, you have one big folder (inDir) that contains data from 1300 cameras over 3 years, all side by side? So no subfolders for the different years?

The Error: inDir contains no station directories.  is probably because the function expects station folders as subfolders of inDir, and gets confused if that's not the case (i.e., you can't replace inDir = "Tagged" with inDir = "Tagged/Camera1" because the station information will be lost.

It should be easy to modify the function though. A few options:
1. "includeStation" argument
2.  "excludeStation" argument
3.  an argument like "stationDirs", which can optionally be used instead of inDir.

Of course one could also combine the functionality of option 3 above with what "inDir" is doing already:
if lenght(inDir) == 1 -> expect station subdirectories
if lenght(inDir) >= 2 -> consider each value in inDir as a station directory

While possible, I think that would be confusing and inconsistent.

What do you think would be best? Personally I favour option 1 (telling the function which stations you want).

Alternatively, the low-tech solution would be to have separate directories for each year and just change inDir accordingly.

Best,
Jürgen

Hi Mariano,

Currently I believe that CamtrapR's base functions do not create hour detection histories. However, you can use the custom function developed by Fabiola Iannarilli in her paper Using lorelograms to measure and model correlation in binary data: Applications to ecological studies <https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/2041-210X.13308> . All the codes and data they used are open and hosted at: https://conservancy.umn.edu/handle/11299/208294
Just download the zip of the data and use the function in the script called "Modified_function_for_detection_histories_by_hour.R"
The arguments are based on the original camtrapR function so it is not that difficult to use. However, if you have a very long sampling (more than 30 days) you will have a huge detection matrix. So sometimes it is useful to make a subset.
I hope you find it helpful.

Best regards,

Even at USB 2 speed it should only take a few hours to copy that amount of data, certainly not several days. If copying is that slow I suppose reading the data has the same problem. source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/master/R/variousOtherHelperFunctions.R" <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/master/R/variousOtherHelperFunctions.R>)

wd_images_ID_species <- system.file("pictures/sample_images_species_dir",

                          IDfrom                 = "directory",

                          writecsv               = FALSE,
                          additionalMetadataTags = c("EXIF:Model", "EXIF:Make"),

Hi Bazilah,

the metadata you shared are for a jpg image, at the top it says:

Metadata of:
D:/video kuala lompat/videoRAW/Beberas/Unknown/PICT0001.JPG

I would suggest you use the fileName argument:
exifTagNames(fileName = "...")

Where you replace ... with the complete path of one of your video files, e.g.
exifTagNames(fileName = "D:/video kuala lompat/videoRAW/video1.avi")

Of course I'm making up the file name, so please adjust that. What you're looking for is an entry in the "value" column that contains the correct date of the video.
When you run recordTable, you can then use it in the video argument as shown above, e.g.

video = list(file_formats = c("jpg", "mov", "avi", "mp4"),
                                      dateTimeTag = "FileModifyDate",
                                      db_directory = "C:/Users/raque/Pictures",
                                      db_filename = "digikam4.db"))

So in Raquel's example, the entry of tag_name was FileModifyDate.
Note that it is more reliable if you combine tag_group and tag_name (separated with a colon), as Raquel has shown above:

For MOV and mp4:  dateTimeTag = "QuickTime:CreateDate"

This is because tags in different groups can have the same names. By specifying the tag_group we make sure R exiftool gets the right values.

Hope this helps. Let us know if it is unclear.
Best regards,
Jürgen

Hi Jürgen
Thank-you for developing such a great package for analysing wildlife survey image data.
We are currently systematically deploying remote cameras to survey small mammals. One of the challenges when tagging images of small mammals is that they cannot always be identified to species level with a high level of confidence. As a result we have tagged our images with a range of tags additional to species including confidence of species ID, mammal group (small, medium, or large mammal, bird or invertebrate), and camera malfunction including misalignment resulting from a bump by a large animal, or glitch in date and time. This means that not all images are tagged with a species id.
I really like the set-up of the output of your record table function. Is there any way to specify for the record table to include all images (and not exclude those without a species ID)?
We would use this information to make an assessment of camera performance (e.g. proportion of images that could be attributed to a given small mammal with high confidence), and perhaps even model the occupancy dynamics of mammal groupings e.g. small mammals.
The code we are using to construct our dataframe is as follows.
Many thanks for your time.

rec.db.species_metadata <- recordTable(inDir = raw_images, IDfrom = "metadata", cameraID = "directory", camerasIndependent = TRUE, metadataSpeciesTag = "Species", metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|", minDeltaTime = 0, timeZone = "Australia/Tasmania", removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE, returnFileNamesMissingTags = TRUE, writecsv = FALSE,additionalMetadataTags = c("EXIF:Model", "EXIF:Make", "metadata_IDConfidenceScore","metadata_Group","metadata_CameraMalfunction"))

apologies for the late reply. Currently you can't make recordTable return records without tags (when using metadata species ID). I believe the easiest solution would be to assign species tags even to those images without an animal in the frame (e.g. "empty", "unknown", or whatever may be the case).

You can use the digiKam "Filters" menu on the right side of the screen to easily list the species without tags (how exactly to do it depends on whether there are other tags assigned already (then "Images Without Tags" won't work), but I'm sure with a little experimentation you can make it work.

After assigning some placeholder species tags to the images without animals, the information of those images will be extracted as if they are species, and can be used in whatever analyses you are planning to do.

Side note, I think you don't need

"metadata_IDConfidenceScore","metadata_Group","metadata_CameraMalfunction")

in additionalMetadataTag. All metdata tags (from digiKam for example) should be extracted automatically.

Best regards,

Jürgen
